[0] everyday_reading (E): Everyday reading: text written in a program is an instruction the computer reads and obeys. Java rule: comments (// to end of line, /* ... */) are ignored by the compiler and have no effect on execution; they are for human readers.
[1] misconception (M) -> CommentIsExecuted: wrong rule: A comment line is run like a statement. Right rule: The compiler ignores comments: everything from // to the end of the line and everything between /* and */.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> CommentIsExecuted: Applies the skip rule unevenly: skips one comment while tracing but 'executes' another (e.g. a commented-out println), or forgets that // ends at the line break. (here mixing in: "A comment line is run like a statement")

[0] names_the_element (N): A comment is explanatory text in the program that the compiler ignores.
[1] states_the_rule (S): A comment is either text between /* and */ or text from // to the end of the line; the compiler ignores it. A comment that starts with /** is a documentation (Javadoc) comment, written before a class or method; tools turn it into API documentation.

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Comments are removed when the source is read by the compiler, so they never take part in execution order; tracing skips them.
[1] output_prediction (OP): A comment produces no value and no output.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): A comment changes no state; adding one and recompiling leaves the program's behaviour identical.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Comments are part of the program text in Name.java but are dropped when it is compiled, so they cannot affect Name.class's behaviour.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Purpose: explain what the code does and why, for other programmers and your future self; also used to disable code temporarily.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> CommentIsExecuted: Adding, removing or editing a comment keeps behaviour unchanged, as long as the delimiters stay intact; deleting a closing */ or turning a statement into a comment changes the program.
[1] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: A /* comment needs its closing */. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: a /* with no matching */: the rest of the file becomes comment, so javac reports an unclosed comment or reached end of file
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: /* and */ are two-character tokens with no space inside. Kind: compile-time. Trigger class: writing / * ... * /: the slashes and stars are read as operators, producing syntax errors
[3] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Use comments to document intent where the code alone is unclear; do not rely on them to change what the program does, and keep them in step with the code.
